 Print (AI image) Twelve individuals boarded the Vande Bharat Express to assist family members, but the doors closed unexpectedly KANPUR: Twelve people who boarded the Kanpur-Delhi Vande Bharat Express to help their relatives settle into their seats were left stranded on the train after its automatic doors shut before they could get off. The group was carried 139 km to Etawah, where the Railway Protection Force (RPF) fined them Rs 3,000 each, collecting a total of Rs 36,000 for travelling without valid tickets. The 12 had entered train no. 22415, running from Banaras to New Delhi, at Kanpur Central to help family members board. However, before they could get off, the train's automatic doors closed and it pulled out of the station. Realising they were on the wrong side of the closed doors, they approached train staff and requested that the doors be opened. However, this was not possible as the train was moving. Vande Bharat's automatic doors can be opened only when the train halts at designated stations and shut after a fixed interval. Women and children were among the 12 people stranded on board. The unexpected journey triggered panic, with some passengers objecting and creating a disturbance. However, the train could not be stopped midway to let them off. Join conversation

 The group finally got off at Etawah, around 139 km from Kanpur. RPF personnel subsequently imposed a fine of Rs 3,000 on each of them for travelling without valid tickets. Shivam Sharma, chief public relations officer of North Central Railway, said unauthorised entry into Vande Bharat coaches was prohibited. He said the 12 had boarded the train without platform tickets while seeing off their relatives. Railway officials took legal action against them after they got off at Etawah and collected a total fine of Rs 36,000 for travelling without valid tickets.
